description: Ran systems/slack-bot/read.py and post.py directly via bash and got 'Tunnel connection failed: 403 Forbidden', then concluded Slack was unreachable and reported the content-discovery run as blocked. David corrected: the scripts run fine, and access to #content should go through the master-slack skill, not raw script invocation in this sandbox.
correction: Use the master-slack skill (as workflow.md specifies: 'Use master-slack skill — systems/slack-bot/post.py via Desktop Commander') instead of running read.py/post.py directly via the bash tool. The bash sandbox has different network access than Desktop Commander/master-slack, so the same script fails differently depending on invocation path.
failure_mode: Used the wrong invocation path for a tool that requires a specific execution context (Desktop Commander via master-slack skill) rather than the general-purpose sandbox shell.
systemic_fix: Before running systems/slack-bot/*.py, read skills/master-slack/SKILL.md and invoke via the specified path (Desktop Commander) rather than mcp__workspace__bash. Do not assume a 403/network error from one execution path means the underlying service is down.
